item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-2ed090a403464d91","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"In December 2023, Sisi secured a third six-year presidential term with 89.6 percent of the reported vote after authorities arrested, intimidated, or otherwise obstructed significant opposition candidates; the report states the process eliminated meaningful competition.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.8","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House attributes the election environment and Sisi's continued power to the Sisi regime and election authorities.","limitations":["Assessment by Freedom House; reported election result is attributed to election authorities."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2ed090a403464d91","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Ahmed Tantawi suspended his presidential campaign after failing to collect the required signatures; more than 10 family members and friends and more than 100 campaign staff were arrested, and Citizen Lab attributed Predator spyware targeting his phone to the Egyptian government with high confidence.","question_ids":["4B.2","4B.3","4B.9","7B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023 election period.","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House attributes the arrests and intimidation to the regime and reports high-confidence attribution of the spyware attack to the Egyptian government.","limitations":["Spyware attribution is reported as high confidence, not as a judicial finding."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2ed090a403464d91","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"The national dialogue opened in May 2023 but excluded the Muslim Brotherhood, produced no significant legal or political reforms, and was paused before the presidential election.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","8B.1","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The dialogue was called by Sisi; Freedom House describes its composition, outcome, and pause.","limitations":["The source does not establish that Sisi personally directed every procedural decision."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2ed090a403464d91","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"The Administrative Control Authority, controlled by Sisi and responsible for most anticorruption initiatives, was described as lacking credibility, transparency, and impartiality and as unable to monitor the military's economic activities.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7","7B.6","7B.9","8B.5"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The institutional finding applies during the 2023 reporting period.","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House directly attributes control of the authority to President Sisi.","limitations":["Institutional assessment rather than a single adjudicated corruption case."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2ed090a403464d91","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"State budget documents were publicly accessible, but debt held by state-owned enterprises was inaccessible, military state-owned-enterprise allocations were omitted, and audits of large state-owned enterprises were not public.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.5","5B.7","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Applies to government transparency during the 2023 report period.","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House attributes the limited transparency to the Sisi administration.","limitations":["The source does not quantify the omitted military allocations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2ed090a403464d91","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"In 2023, 24 journalists were reported imprisoned by the Egyptian Journalists Syndicate; at least 562 websites and links, including at least 132 journalistic websites, had been blocked, and authorities censored online content without judicial approval.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 conditions and reported cumulative blocking.","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House attributes the censorship, arrests, and website blocking to Egyptian authorities under Sisi.","limitations":["The website total is cumulative and not limited to blocks imposed during 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2ed090a403464d91","start_unit":10,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"From early 2023 through mid-September, security forces arrested more than 2,000 people for peaceful expression or assembly; at least 100 more were arrested in October for pro-Palestinian protests.","question_ids":["3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House attributes the arrests to Egyptian security forces under the Sisi government.","limitations":["The first figure comes from an independent campaign cited by Freedom House."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2ed090a403464d91","start_unit":12,"end_unit":13,"fact_summary":"The executive influenced courts; military courts tried civilians under broad jurisdiction; prison conditions included overcrowding, abuse, medical neglect, and deaths in custody; and no prosecutions were undertaken for the 2013 Rabaa killings by the 2023 anniversary.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.9","4B.4","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The findings describe conditions continuing into 2023, with some historical context.","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House attributes executive influence, security-force impunity, and the lack of Rabaa accountability to Sisi-era authorities.","limitations":["Some quantitative death-penalty figures cover the decade before 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c8ad3f5f524f7c7f","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The 2023 State Department report identified credible reports of arbitrary killings, enforced disappearance, torture, life-threatening prison conditions, arbitrary detention, judicial interference, restrictions on expression, assembly, association, political participation, corruption, and gender-based violence; it also stated that most abuse allegations were not comprehensively investigated or prosecuted.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.4","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report evaluates the Egyptian government during Sisi's presidency.","limitations":["The executive summary aggregates many source reports and does not assign each allegation to Sisi personally."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c8ad3f5f524f7c7f","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"A domestic torture-monitoring group documented approximately 2,700 violations of prisoners' rights through the first three quarters of 2023; rights groups described torture as institutionalized and enabled by counterterrorism law, incommunicado detention, and impunity.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the practices to police, prison guards, and the legal and institutional framework of the Egyptian government.","limitations":["The 2,700 figure is from a domestic rights group and covers reported violations, not necessarily adjudicated incidents."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c8ad3f5f524f7c7f","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Authorities regularly used prolonged pretrial detention and added or recycled charges to extend detention; in a 2022 sample, terrorism-circuit detention renewals occurred in 98.6 percent of more than 25,000 hearings, and video hearings were expanded in 2023.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","4B.4","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The practice continued into the 2023 reporting year; the quantitative sample is from 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the detention practices to Egyptian prosecutors, courts, and security authorities.","limitations":["The 98.6 percent statistic is for 2022, not 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c8ad3f5f524f7c7f","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"In 2023, the government monitored communications and used spyware against critics; Citizen Lab and media reported Ahmed Tantawy's phone was hacked repeatedly with Predator spyware between May and September, while surveillance lacked transparency and was not consistently supported by judicial warrants.","question_ids":["4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes surveillance operations to Egyptian security agencies and reports likely government involvement in Tantawy's targeting.","limitations":["The Tantawy attribution is reported as an allegation supported by high-confidence technical assessment, not a court judgment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c8ad3f5f524f7c7f","start_unit":10,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"In October 2023, security forces arrested more than 100 people for unauthorized protests, including pro-Palestinian demonstrations; the government also used restrictive assembly laws and violently dispersed gatherings.","question_ids":["2B.6","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the arrests and dispersals to Egyptian security forces and government policy.","limitations":["The report does not identify the individual officials who ordered each arrest."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c8ad3f5f524f7c7f","start_unit":13,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"The December 2023 presidential election was widely reported as unfair; opposition supporters were assaulted, threatened, or intimidated while collecting endorsements, and Tantawy reported more than 100 campaign volunteers, supporters, and family members arrested before the filing deadline.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023 election.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the controlled election environment and arrests to Egyptian authorities under Sisi.","limitations":["Some arrest totals are reported claims by Tantawy and rights groups."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c8ad3f5f524f7c7f","start_unit":14,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"In 2023, six women led cabinet ministries, two Christians served among 27 appointed governors, and Sisi appointed at least 45 judges, including the first woman appointed to the State Council's Disciplinary Court.","question_ids":["4B.7","4B.4","8B.4"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns appointments reported for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the appointments to President Sisi and the Egyptian government.","limitations":["The fact demonstrates representation or appointment activity but does not establish institutional independence or performance."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c8ad3f5f524f7c7f","start_unit":15,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"The government operated an antiviolence unit in the Interior Ministry, a National Council for Women, FGM hotlines, and a February 2023 public-awareness campaign; authorities also reported blocking attempted FGM cases and stopping attempted child marriages.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.3","6B.8","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns measures reported during 2023, with outcome data partly historical.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the institutions and measures to the Egyptian government under Sisi.","limitations":["The report also states enforcement remained incomplete and gender-based violence remained widespread."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c8ad3f5f524f7c7f","start_unit":16,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"Sisi announced a policy encouraging smaller families and a 1,000 EGP annual incentive for married women who limited themselves to two children, alongside free or reduced-cost family-planning methods.","question_ids":["5B.1","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns a September 2023 policy announcement.","ruler_attribution":"The report directly attributes the policy and public statement to President Sisi.","limitations":["The incentive was payable only after the woman turned 45 if conditions were met; no outcome data are supplied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fcd9b8664961ccf5","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"In July 2024, authorities detained 119 people, including women and a child, over online calls for anti-government protests tied to rising prices and power cuts; detainees were charged with terrorism-related offenses and held pending investigation. The report states electricity cuts had been imposed since July 2023.","question_ids":["3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.9","5B.9","6B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The protest arrests occurred in 2024; the power-cut policy began in 2023, so this is only partly period-fit for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Amnesty attributes the detentions and cost-saving measures to Egyptian authorities and Sisi's government.","limitations":["The arrests post-date the target period and should not be treated as 2023 events."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1ad8cf1f7dfb6300","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that Sisi's government maintained zero tolerance for dissent, used repressive NGO legislation, and allowed near-absolute impunity for security-force abuses; in 2017 security forces carried out arbitrary detention, disappearance, torture, and alleged extrajudicial killings.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","4B.3","6B.7","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Historical evidence from 2017 provides background for institutional conditions continuing into 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report directly attributes the policy and abuses to Sisi's government.","limitations":["The documented events predate 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1ad8cf1f7dfb6300","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"In 2017, authorities blocked more than 425 websites, imprisoned journalists, criminalized peaceful gatherings, arrested activists before anticipated protests, and Sisi pardoned 705 prisoners, most convicted in peaceful-protest cases.","question_ids":["3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Historical evidence from 2017; the pardon is favorable but the broader pattern predates 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Human Rights Watch attributes the repression and pardons to Sisi and his government.","limitations":["The facts do not establish that the 2017 measures remained unchanged in every detail in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3ef86388721ced43","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch documented systematic arbitrary arrests, enforced disappearances, torture, extrajudicial killings, collective punishment, forced evictions, and possible unlawful attacks by Egyptian forces in North Sinai; it also documented serious abuses by ISIS-affiliated militants.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.6","3B.9","6B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The report primarily concerns 2015–2017, with some incidents through 2018; it is historical context for 2023 security policy.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes government-force abuses to Egyptian military and police forces and separately attributes abuses to Sinai Province militants.","limitations":["The report is not a 2023 assessment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3ef86388721ced43","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"The army recruited, armed, paid, and directed irregular North Sinai militias that had de facto arrest powers; residents reported militia members used operations to settle personal disputes or advance business interests, and Human Rights Watch found no evidence of accountability for abusive members.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.5","2B.9","3B.2","7B.9","8B.3","8B.5"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Historical evidence from 2015–2018 relevant to the security apparatus inherited in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Human Rights Watch attributes the militias' organization and direction to the Egyptian military under Sisi-era policy.","limitations":["The source states the government did not officially acknowledge or regulate the militias."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3ef86388721ced43","start_unit":16,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"After the 2017 Rawda Mosque attack, Sisi ordered the military to secure Sinai within three months and publicly instructed commanders to use 'all brute force'; subsequent operations included arrests, killings, demolitions, and large-scale displacement.","question_ids":["2B.2","2B.3","2B.4","2B.8","3B.9","6B.6","8B.1","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Historical directive and subsequent effects, relevant to the security program continuing into 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Human Rights Watch directly attributes the directive to President Sisi.","limitations":["The source reports a public order but does not provide a complete implementation record for 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3ef86388721ced43","start_unit":19,"end_unit":20,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch concluded that Egyptian authorities repeatedly violated safeguards against arbitrary detention, torture, and extrajudicial execution in North Sinai; the 2015 counterterrorism law granted security personnel immunity from criminal investigation for lethal force, and Law 161 of 2018 restricted prosecution of senior commanders without armed-forces approval.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Historical legal and institutional findings relevant to the posture entering 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the laws and security practices to the Egyptian state and identifies Sisi's approval of Law 161.","limitations":["The findings concern laws and conduct documented before 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3ef86388721ced43","start_unit":23,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch documented 50 arbitrary-arrest cases in North Sinai, including 39 likely enforced disappearances; most families received no official acknowledgment, judicial review, or response to complaints, and no compensation was identified for detainees released after secret detention.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.9","6B.7","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Historical evidence from 2013–2018 relevant to enduring institutional practices.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the arrests and lack of remedy to Egyptian army, police, and security authorities.","limitations":["The sample is based on documented cases and is not a national census."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3ef86388721ced43","start_unit":31,"end_unit":33,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch documented at least 14 extrajudicial killings of detainees in North Sinai and found no evidence that prosecutors investigated the cases; official statements allegedly presented some victims as militants killed in clashes after detention.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.9","7B.1","7B.2","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Historical evidence from 2014–2018 relevant to accountability institutions in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the killings and investigation failures to Egyptian security forces and prosecutors.","limitations":["The report documents cases through interviews and media/video review rather than final judicial findings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3ef86388721ced43","start_unit":43,"end_unit":44,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch interviewed families reporting 15 army attacks that damaged or destroyed homes or killed or injured relatives; 11 children and 6 women were among those killed, compensation was opaque, and prosecutors did not investigate the cases.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.9","3B.7","3B.9","6B.6","6B.7","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Historical evidence from 2014–2018 relevant to conflict policy and remedy mechanisms.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the attacks and compensation process to the Egyptian army and government.","limitations":["Several incidents involved ongoing clashes, and the source reports possible unlawfulness rather than definitive court findings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3bd6324b2ffac337","start_unit":12,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"RSF's 2019 Media Ownership Monitor found that nearly all major Egyptian media were controlled by the state, intelligence services, or regime-aligned businessmen; Egyptian Media Group had made at least a dozen forced acquisitions since 2016, and its director was appointed by the president and controlled by intelligence services.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.5","4B.6","7B.5","7B.9","8B.3","8B.5"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Institutional evidence from 2019 relevant to media conditions continuing into 2023.","ruler_attribution":"RSF attributes the consolidation and legislative changes to the state under President Sisi.","limitations":["The source is from 2019, not a 2023 ownership audit."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d956605444721641","start_unit":3,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"The Cambridge chapter's accessible summary states that Egypt's presidents have pursued distinct strategic styles and places Sisi's current strategic priorities in historical perspective, but the supplied excerpt does not provide a specific 2023 Sisi policy, event, or outcome.","question_ids":[],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Published 2025 and summarized a chapter published in 2021; not a direct 2023 evidence source.","ruler_attribution":"The summary concerns presidential foreign-policy styles generally and does not provide a concrete 2023 Sisi attribution.","limitations":["Full chapter access was unavailable in the supplied document; no concrete 2023 fact is extracted."]},{"source_id":"SRC-edb621ae587c7f28","start_unit":14,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"Sisi won a third six-year term in December 2023 with 89.6 percent of the reported vote after authorities prevented Ahmed Tantawy from qualifying; the parliament was described as pro-Sisi and as having rubber-stamped 2019 amendments extending presidential power.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.8","8B.1","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023 election and the constitutional framework governing it.","ruler_attribution":"Human Rights Watch attributes the election restrictions and constitutional entrenchment to Sisi's government and parliament.","limitations":["The reported vote share is attributed to authorities."]},{"source_id":"SRC-edb621ae587c7f28","start_unit":16,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"By November 2023, at least 127 Tantawy supporters and volunteers had been detained; authorities also detained about 2,028 people from early 2023 through mid-September for peaceful expression or assembly, releasing only 627 according to an independent campaign.","question_ids":["3B.8","4B.3","4B.9","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Human Rights Watch attributes the detentions to Egyptian security and prosecutorial authorities under Sisi.","limitations":["The 2,028 and 627 figures are attributed to an independent campaign."]},{"source_id":"SRC-edb621ae587c7f28","start_unit":17,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"In 2023, the Supreme Media Regulatory Council referred Mada Masr staff for prosecution, authorities prosecuted journalists, and at least two independent news websites were blocked amid a broader pattern of hundreds of blocked websites.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Human Rights Watch attributes the prosecutions and blocking to Egyptian authorities.","limitations":["The article reports allegations and institutional actions, not final convictions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-edb621ae587c7f28","start_unit":18,"end_unit":20,"fact_summary":"Authorities detained and prosecuted people solely for supporting Tantawy, obstructed endorsement registration at notary offices, tolerated physical harassment by pro-Sisi supporters, and did not investigate at least one complaint about intimidation.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.9","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns September–October 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Human Rights Watch attributes the obstruction and arrests to security agencies and reports intimidation by pro-Sisi actors.","limitations":["Some physical attacks were by unidentified or nonstate actors; police nonintervention is reported by witnesses."]},{"source_id":"SRC-858d3dcc2e6141e5","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"During the 2023 reporting period, internet access expanded to 82.01 million users and 72.2 percent penetration, while government investment and Telecom Egypt projects expanded fiber and international cable infrastructure; daily one- to two-hour power cuts from July 2023 disrupted fixed and mobile connectivity.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.9","6B.2","6B.6","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns infrastructure and access during 2023 and the surrounding coverage period.","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House attributes infrastructure investment and load-shedding to Egyptian government institutions and Telecom Egypt.","limitations":["Some infrastructure projects began before 2023 or were completed after the target year."]},{"source_id":"SRC-858d3dcc2e6141e5","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"Inflation reached 34.6 percent in November 2023, negatively affecting internet affordability; ADSL subscriptions were concentrated in Cairo and the Nile Delta, while Sinai, the Red Sea, and the Suez Canal collectively accounted for only 6 percent.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 economic and regional access conditions.","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House reports national economic and infrastructure conditions under the Sisi government.","limitations":["The regional subscription figures are from January 2024 and are used as a near-period indicator."]},{"source_id":"SRC-858d3dcc2e6141e5","start_unit":15,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"The NTRA is subordinated to the communications ministry and its board includes defense, interior, presidency, and security representatives; in 2023 it imposed a 20 million EGP fine on Telecom Egypt after a nationwide service disruption.","question_ids":["4B.4","5B.3","5B.7","8B.4","8B.5","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns institutional structure and a December 2023 enforcement action.","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House attributes the regulatory structure to Egyptian law and the fine to the NTRA.","limitations":["The fine is a favorable enforcement action but does not establish broader regulator independence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-858d3dcc2e6141e5","start_unit":17,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"During the coverage period, Egypt blocked 562 websites, including about 132 news websites; in June 2023 authorities blocked Soulta 4 and Masr 360, and in October announced a six-month block of Mada Masr after a report about possible Palestinian displacement.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 blocking actions and cumulative totals reported in 2024.","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House attributes the blocking to the NTRA, SCMR, and Egyptian authorities.","limitations":["The 562 total is as of June 2024, not a 2023-only count."]},{"source_id":"SRC-858d3dcc2e6141e5","start_unit":25,"end_unit":27,"fact_summary":"The information environment was dominated by government-affiliated or pro-government outlets; August 2023 analysis identified Youm7 as a leading promoter of misinformation and found that election coverage showed pro-Sisi bias while opposition politicians were denied or criticized.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","7B.1","7B.2","7B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 information conditions.","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House attributes the media environment and pro-government influence to state officials and government-connected actors.","limitations":["The Youm7 finding concerns misinformation analysis, not a judicial determination of intentional deception."]},{"source_id":"SRC-858d3dcc2e6141e5","start_unit":32,"end_unit":33,"fact_summary":"Ahead of the December 2023 election, authorities detained at least 73 Tantawy campaign members or volunteers and charged several with terrorism-related offenses, false news, or misuse of social media; Tantawy's phone was infected with Predator spyware.","question_ids":["4B.2","4B.3","4B.9","7B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023 election period.","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House attributes the repression to Egyptian security services and reports likely security-service involvement in the spyware attack.","limitations":["The 73 figure is from EIPR; spyware attribution is described as likely."]},{"source_id":"SRC-858d3dcc2e6141e5","start_unit":42,"end_unit":45,"fact_summary":"In 2023, Mohamed Ali received a life sentence in absentia for online mobilization; Patrick George Zaki received a three-year sentence for an online article and was then pardoned; Hisham Kassem received six months for social-media criticism; and Oxygen remained detained after his sentence expired.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","4B.3","7B.2","7B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 cases, with some continuing historical detention context.","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House attributes the prosecutions to Egyptian authorities and the pardon to President Sisi.","limitations":["The pardon is favorable for one detainee but does not establish general correction of abusive prosecutions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-858d3dcc2e6141e5","start_unit":52,"end_unit":54,"fact_summary":"Between May and September 2023, Ahmed Tantawi's phone was infected with Predator spyware capable of accessing the microphone, camera, contacts, and messages; Citizen Lab attributed the attack to the Egyptian government with high confidence based on technical evidence and Egypt's record as a Cytrox customer.","question_ids":["4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Citizen Lab and Freedom House report high-confidence attribution to the Egyptian government.","limitations":["High-confidence technical attribution is not a final court finding."]},{"source_id":"SRC-858d3dcc2e6141e5","start_unit":57,"end_unit":58,"fact_summary":"Egyptian law required providers to retain user data for 180 days and allowed state agencies to request stored data without judicial orders; in the second half of 2023 Google received two emergency disclosure requests and Meta received 12 requests concerning 14 accounts.","question_ids":["4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The legal regime and company requests cover 2023;
